status: PASS for the precise strict real-PL recognition and arbitrary-current multiplier theorem; original P21.3 remains open

report.report:
The supplied argument establishes the precise strict real-PL theorem, including the multiplier identity for every stated ordinary current and the fixed-neighbourhood locally uniform net closure. This certification excludes universal P21.3, trivial valuation, the broader integral-parlinear class, and Psh ∩ C = CPsh. I checked the applications against [CLD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2) and [GJR v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.05741v3), without treating the book or previous reviews as premises.

The strictness checks succeed. GJR 5.8 supplies an ordinary-local finite presentation, rather than merely a G-local one. Rational independence, rational tropical directions, rigid-point values in QΓ, and finite denominator clearing justify its gluing step. Formal metric realization and common dominance apply on the compact strict neighbourhoods used here, without reducedness or discrete valuation. The residue identifications concern degree-one strict reductions. Properness follows from the inner-point condition. Strict lifting supplies an analytically trivial line-bundle germ with genuinely strictly integral weight; it does not introduce an arbitrary real normalization constant.

The model comparisons also succeed. Finite transition data and their isomorphisms descend through the filtered model system. Proper pullback and surjective descent of nefness follow from the curve projection formula; a curve downstairs is dominated by the closure of a closed point over its generic point. Consequently the real residue classes can be compared on one model. The projective nef-plus-ample application has the required arbitrary-field scope. Its passage from numerical ampleness to the real-Picard definition uses a rational cube in the finite coefficient space, so the resulting classes are actual nonnegative combinations of ample line bundles.

All five supporting lemmas check out. Lemma 1's successive minimal-sheaf arguments establish scaling and addition; restriction compatibility follows by extending a candidate subsheaf from an open to the ambient space. Compact neighbourhood interiors handle locally uniform sequential convergence. The corrected decreasing subsequence proves the safe CPsh ⊂ Psh inclusion, including the zero-error case, without Proposition 8.1.11. Lemma 2's soft maximum has the stated positive covariance Hessian and the global error bound τ log r. The strict semiample lifting and zero-residue kernel justify its local presentation, including the smooth logarithmic remainder.

For Lemma 3, middle positivity suffices throughout. Positive-test decomposition produces scalar Radon measures and the stated supremum estimate. Independence from the decomposition follows by smooth scalar approximation. On each finite moment presentation, domination by a fixed positive coefficient form also supplies the order-zero continuity required for the product to be a current. This avoids the erroneous strongly-positive spanning claim. Both closedness equations remove the mixed Leibniz terms; uniform limits preserve positivity; distributional identities give double closedness. Positive-test decomposition and symmetry prove pointedness in every complementary degree, including scalar tests.

Lemma 4 fixes all models and class identifications before choosing η. On O = Int_X(Z) ∩ red_Z⁻¹(V′), pullback and restriction of the semiample class apply at every point of the same open. Boundedness of b on compact Z gives uniform convergence there. Thus the reconstruction of GJR 7.10 has no approximation-dependent neighbourhood. Lemma 5 then gives one strictly integral a, one integer N, and one bounded ordinary B for all finitely many inequalities. No strict positivity of dd[a] beyond these inequalities is needed.

The rational-recognition identity is algebraically correct, and every term on its right is a positive ordinary current. Clearing denominators preserves strict integrality. Recognition can be applied at every point of the fixed B; intermediate neighbourhoods may depend on the index because membership is subsequently glued by the sheaf property. The final convergence is uniform on the original B. Residual nefness follows independently by taking limits against each fixed proper curve on the common model; no finite curve test is assumed.

I traced the essential positive-to-nef implication through CLD 18.8.4, 17.6.4–5, 18.6.1, and the degree-one mass calculation. A residual curve's generic tube accumulates at the original point, so it meets the positivity neighbourhood. The characteristic-exponent power gives analytic definition dimension at most one, and the flat fibre formula turns its degree into a curvature coefficient with strictly positive multiplicity factors. The calibrated-cone comparison has the requisite Abhyankar hypotheses. Its auxiliary functions can be chosen in the dense algebraic function field, making the ACVF finite-fibre formula algebraic; the infinitesimal valuation comparison has the required arbitrary-rank defectlessness scope.

The identified inference in CLD 16.7.5 is indeed invalid in general: z is a non-zero-divisor in k[x,y,z]/(x²,xy), although the ring has the embedded associated prime (x,y) and fails S1. The needed degree-one source calculation does not depend on that inference. It decomposes the algebraic cycle into integral components before invoking Poincaré–Lelong. Those analytifications satisfy S1 independently, and the conditional proof has its hypothesis established. Generic nilpotent multiplicities are retained in the subsequent analytic mass and fibre calculations. No Poincaré–Lelong assertion on an embedded-prime source is silently granted.

For zero current, both signs are CPsh, so both signs of dd(hT) are positive and pointedness gives zero. The compact-support estimate works for the original directed net on a fixed neighbourhood, with its compact set and constant independent of the index. Linearity then yields the U,V identity using only their certified difference; no reclassification of U or V is necessary.

The worked surface is valid. The Gauss point has residue C(E), and the normal proper curve E is cofinal among its reduction models, giving Pic(red(C,x)) = Pic(E). Abel–Jacobi makes O_E(z−o) non-torsion, while its degree and its inverse's degree are zero. The supporting lemmas' proofs also apply in dimension one, as required for this preliminary curve construction. If g were smooth, rational-affine recognition and its strict rigid-point values would make an integer multiple an ordinary analytic-unit logarithm, contradicting non-torsion. The analytic product with the open disc is a strict smooth boundaryless surface. CPsh pullback is justified directly by minimality, and its analytic section proves nonsmoothness without pulling back a current equation.

Harmless corrections: G1 must say that the logarithmic PL functions glue; the units themselves need not glue. In GJR 6.11's final descent sentence the intended representative is the given model's class. CLD 18.4.5's displayed maximum formulas require the logarithms indicated by the preceding metric formula. These corrections require no substantial change to the supplied proof. The workspace/hash/compiler assertions were not mathematical premises of this certification.

passages.statement: On a good, separated, pure-dimensional analytic space over a complete non-Archimedean field, CLD's canonical calibrated tropical structure agrees with restriction to analytic domains. Its boundaryless ordinary opens have ordinary sheaves of forms and currents, compact-support smooth localization, smooth scalar approximation, and Stokes. The fundamental current retains generic component multiplicities and is positive and doubly closed. Analytic-unit logarithms are smooth with zero smooth Hessian. Analytification of a finite-type scheme has regular local structure maps. CLD §§6.2, 7.1, 11.1.11, 15.7 and 16.6.

CLD Definition 8.1.7 defines CPsh as the smallest ordinary subsheaf of finite continuous functions containing smooth functions with positive smooth Hessian and closed under uniform sequential limits on each fixed open. Definition 8.1.1 defines Psh by smooth positive-Hessian generators and decreasing sequential limits with locally integrable limit.

For compactly supported ordinary smooth tests on good boundaryless analytic spaces, every symmetric (q,q)-test is a difference of two compactly supported middle-positive tests. Wedges of middle-positive forms are middle-positive. Pairing a middle-positive current with a complementary positive form defines a positive Radon measure, and locally bounded continuous functions have the ordinary order-zero product with such currents. CLD 6.5.2, 3.5.5, 7.2.7–12; GJR 7.12.

Over a complete nontrivially valued field, GJR real-PL functions on good strict analytic spaces use the G-topology generated by strict affinoid domains and finite real combinations of analytic-unit logarithms. Every such function is ordinary-locally a finite real sum of integral PL functions and has arbitrarily small compact strict neighbourhoods admitting a common formal presentation. GJR 5.1, 5.8 and 5.9.

On a paracompact separated strict analytic space over a complete nontrivially valued field, a metric is formal exactly when it is integral PL. Admissible formal models admit common blowup dominance; finite strict domain covers and morphisms between compact strict domains can be realized on compatible formal models after admissible blowups. Gubler–Martin 2019, Proposition 2.10; Bosch's Raynaud theorem and formal covering lemmas.

For a quasi-compact open of a Riemann–Zariski space, models in GJR's sense are filtered, and its Picard group is the filtered colimit of model Picard groups, also after tensoring with R. Nefness means nonnegative degree on every proper integral curve and can be checked on any representing model. Pullback preserves nefness; proper surjective pullback also detects it; field extension preserves and detects nefness. GJR 6.2, 6.5–6.11.

For a good strict analytic germ over a complete nontrivially valued field, the integral PL residue is intrinsic and represented by restriction of its formal line bundle to the reduction closure. Residues extend additively and real-linearly to real-PL germs. The kernel of the real residue map consists exactly of finite real combinations of ordinary analytic-unit logarithms. These strict residues agree with CLD's degree-one residual bundles. GJR 6.13, 6.16–6.18; CLD 17.5 and 17.7.10.

For a good strict analytic germ over a complete nontrivially valued field, formal reduction closures of compact strict neighbourhoods are cofinal among reduction models. For a real-PL function, nefness of its residue at a point is equivalent to a nearby nef real formal presentation; its semipositive locus is ordinary open. GJR 6.14, 7.1 and 7.3(4).

On a separated, almost-good strict analytic germ, every residual line bundle lifts to a strictly integral metrized analytic line-bundle germ whose underlying bundle is analytically trivial near the point. Degree-one residual frames and transition isomorphisms lift after finite shrinking. A globally generated residual bundle gives a finite logarithmic-maximum weight after frame normalization; a semiample bundle gives this after a positive tensor power, with analytic-unit logarithmic frame terms. CLD 17.5.3–10.

Degree-one residual frames and transition isomorphisms lift after finite shrinking. A globally generated residual bundle gives a finite logarithmic-maximum weight after frame normalization; a semiample bundle gives this after a positive tensor power, with analytic-unit logarithmic frame terms. CLD 17.5.3–10.
For a separated admissible formal model of a compact strict analytic space, the reduced closure of the reduction of an inner analytic point is proper over the residue field. CLD Lemma 11.9.2(d).
Every proper integral variety over an arbitrary field admits a proper birational morphism from a projective integral variety. Chow's lemma.

For an ample line bundle A and any line bundle M on a projective variety over an arbitrary field, A^N ⊗ M is ample for every sufficiently large integer N. Serre's global-generation theorem and the very-ample tensor-product criterion.

On a projective variety over an arbitrary field, a nef class M in Pic ⊗ R plus ε[A], with A an ample integral line bundle and ε > 0, is ample in the sense of a finite nonnegative real combination of ample integral line bundles. Integral ampleness is preserved and detected by field extension. Lazarsfeld, Corollary 1.4.10 and Remark 1.4.34; fpqc descent of ampleness.

On a projective variety over an arbitrary field, a nef class M in Pic ⊗ R plus ε[A], with A an ample integral line bundle and ε > 0, is ample in the sense of a finite nonnegative real combination of ample integral line bundles. Integral ampleness is preserved and detected by field extension. Lazarsfeld, Corollary 1.4.10 and Remark 1.4.34; fpqc descent of ampleness.

On a good, separated, strict, boundaryless pure-dimensional analytic space over a complete nontrivially valued field, positivity near x of the first Chern current of a strictly integral metrized line bundle implies nefness of its strict residual line bundle at x. For the trivial bundle with norm exp(−b), its first Chern current is dd[b]. CLD 18.8.4 with d = 1 and 18.1.2.

For an integral metrized line bundle on a boundaryless analytic curve, the degree-one curvature coefficient at a strict Abhyankar point is its residual intersection degree multiplied by strictly positive analytic multiplicity and graded field-degree factors. Under a flat boundaryless morphism from a pure-dimensional analytic space, the pulled-back degree-one curvature is the corresponding sum of coefficients times the canonical integration currents of the analytic fibres. CLD 18.4.3–7 and 18.6.1.

Over an algebraically closed complete non-Archimedean field, let (X,x) be a boundaryless, generically quasi-smooth, pure n-dimensional analytic germ with d_K(x) = n. For analytic units of norm one at x, their tropical dimensions agree with those of their reductions on a proper variety with function field tilde H(x)_1; when that dimension is n, the calibrated tropical cones agree. CLD Theorem 14.6.2.
If a valued function field F/K has no transcendence defect and K is defectless, then F is defectless; no rank-one restriction is imposed. Kuhlmann, Generalized Stability Theorem, Theorem 1.1.
The theory of algebraically closed nontrivially valued fields eliminates quantifiers in the field language augmented by valuation divisibility. Robinson's ACVF quantifier-elimination theorem.

passages.statement: For an integral algebraic curve over a complete non-Archimedean field, its analytification satisfies S1, and the ordinary Poincaré–Lelong identity holds for a nonzero rational function: dd[log|f|] equals the integration current of its principal divisor, interpreted locally by differences at poles. CLD 11.1.11 and the S1 case of the proof in 16.7.3–5.

If an integral PL function is ordinary CLD-smooth near a point of a good separated analytic space, then on an ordinary neighbourhood some positive integer multiple equals c + log|u| for a real constant c and an analytic unit u. This is the first assertion of CLD Proposition 12.5.4.

For an elliptic curve E over C with origin o, the map z ↦ O_E(z−o) identifies E(C) with Pic^0(E) as groups, and E(C)[m] is finite for every positive integer m. The Abel–Jacobi theorem and the elliptic torsion theorem.

For an elliptic curve E over C with origin o, the map z ↦ O_E(z−o) identifies E(C) with Pic^0(E) as groups, and E(C)[m] is finite for every positive integer m. The Abel–Jacobi theorem and the elliptic torsion theorem.

For finitely many strictly integral metrized line-bundle germs with analytically trivial underlying bundles on a good separated strict germ, residual definition dimension d implies that a common power q, a power of the residue characteristic exponent, has analytic definition dimension at most d. The defining morphism is flat and boundaryless, with a strict target quasi-étale over a torus of dimension at most d. CLD 17.6.4(c) and its strict variant 17.6.5.
For the reduction map π of an affinoid analytic space and a point ξ of its reduction, the closure of π⁻¹(ξ) is the union of π⁻¹(η) over all generizations η of ξ. CLD Lemma 11.7.2.

reviewed_scope: Prove and independently audit the full strict real-PL recognition and ordinary Bedford--Taylor multiplier argument supplied. The main function class is the actual GJR real-PL class over a complete NONTRIVIALLY valued K, on every ordinary open in a good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic space, n>=2. Positive ordinary Hessian current, residual nefness, and CPsh membership must be equivalent in this exact class. Zero-current functions must give dd(hT)=0 for every arbitrary positive doubly closed ordinary CLD current of every target degree, with the stated fixed-neighbourhood locally uniform NET closure. Also audit all five supporting lemmas, direct minimal-sheaf facts, the fixed-neighbourhood reconstruction of GJR 7.10, the genuine strictly integral order unit, and the actual nonsmooth analytic surface worked test. No merely integral CLD parlinear class or full Psh/C-intersection equality is claimed. Incoming finite continuous U,V need not themselves be reclassified as CPsh to obtain their identity from the certified difference class.
post_review_edits: Add the actual independent limited PASS provenance to the paper header; no formal-verification or priority claim.
Clarify, as explicitly requested in the PASS report, that logarithmic PL functions glue, while their analytic units need not glue.
paper_build_input: The exact frozen independently reviewed argument, rather than the later drafting-worker expansion of the product-continuity explanation.
uncertified_broader_claims: General integral-parlinear recognition, full finite Psh/CPsh equality, arbitrary continuous equal-curvature differences, and trivial valuation are not certified.
